_comment: Developed on the dev conversations c01 to c04 only. Each version and what changed is listed in history.

history.change: After v1 on c01-c04. Summary: v1 copied the transcript word for word, hit the 300-token cap in 14 of 16 calls, and stopped taking in later turns; v2 moves the instructions into the user message, asks for short notes in the model's own words, carries earlier facts over, and asks for at most 150 words. Extraction: v1's issue drifted to 'unknown' and its status changed on most turns and ended 'resolved' when the customer said thanks; v2 says to copy fields unless the turn gives a new value, defines when status changes and when the case is resolved, and limits issue changes to the listed values. Answer: v1 invented amounts (in pounds) that the context didn't have; v2 says not to guess details and that a summary or case record at the start is part of the conversation.

After v2 on c01-c04, the last round (stopping rule: afterwards any prompt that reads worse than in v2 goes back to its v2 text, then the prompts are frozen). Summary: v2 ignored the 150-word limit and appended on every update, so 3 of 4 final summaries were cut off at the 300-token cap and lost the newest turns; c03 repeated one line eight times and kept a stale issue; c01 gained an invented preference. v3 asks for a rewrite as at most 15 notes, each one useful fact, updating a note in place when its fact changes, never repeating a note, and never inferring a preference or fact. Extraction: v2's status changed on most turns ('waiting for customer' whenever the assistant asked anything, 'return label sent' with no label, 'resolved' after thanks) and the issue drifted or was misread (c04 'wrong item' for a missing glass). v3 defines every issue value and ties each status change to an explicit statement by the assistant. Answer prompt unchanged.

Frozen by the stopping rule after reading v3 on c01-c04. The v3 summary prompt read worse than v2 (c01 repeated the order number on every other line, c03 copied the transcript again, c02 invented a failed delivery, and every summary from turns 1-8 on was cut off at the cap and stopped changing), so the summary prompt is v2's. The v3 extraction prompt read better than v2 (final records right in 9 of 12 fields against 6; fewer status changes), so it is kept. The answer prompt is unchanged since v2. Remaining known faults, not tuned further: summaries outgrow the 300-token cap and are cut off; status still becomes 'resolved' at the end of three of four dev conversations and 'return label sent' where no label was sent; answers can invent values the context lacks.

system: You are the support assistant for Fernwick Goods, an online homeware shop. Answer the customer's last message using only what this conversation says, including any summary or case record at the start of it. Keep the answer short. Don't guess: if a detail such as a number, date, amount, or code isn't in the conversation, say that you don't have that information.
summary_block:
Summary of the earlier part of this conversation:
{summary}
state_block:
Case record for this conversation, kept up to date after every turn:
{state}
summary_system: You keep a running summary of a customer support chat at Fernwick Goods, an online homeware shop. The summary replaces the earlier turns: the assistant will know only what the summary says.
extraction_system:
You keep the case record of a customer support chat at Fernwick Goods, an online homeware shop. After each turn you receive the current record and the latest turn, and you return the updated record as JSON. Each field holds its current value only. Copy each field from the current record unless the latest turn clearly gives it a new value; a turn that doesn't mention a field leaves it unchanged.
- order_id: the order number the conversation is about, FW- followed by five digits. If the customer corrects it, use the corrected number. An empty string until one is given.
- issue: what is wrong with the order. 'unknown' until it is clear; change it only if the turn shows that the problem is a different one of these:
  damaged: the item arrived broken, cracked, or otherwise damaged.
  wrong item: a different product, colour, or variant arrived from the one ordered.
  missing item: the order, or part of it, never arrived.
  wrong size: the right product arrived in the wrong size.
  late delivery: the order hasn't arrived by its expected date and is still on its way.
  not refunded: a refund the customer is owed hasn't reached them.
  double charged: the customer was charged more than once for the same order.
- status: where the case stands. Change it only when the assistant's message in the latest turn says one of these:
  waiting for customer: the assistant asks the customer to send or do something the case can't go on without, such as photos or the right order number. An ordinary question doesn't count.
  return label sent: the assistant says it has sent or emailed a return label.
  replacement sent: the assistant says a replacement or exchange has shipped.
  refund issued: the assistant says a refund has been sent or issued.
  escalated: the assistant says it has passed the case to another team, or that the courier is investigating.
  resolved: the assistant says the case is closed or resolved.
  'new' is only the starting value. Answering questions, giving advice, and the customer's thanks or goodbye don't change the status.
